subject: Agriculture
title: Qanat Systems
description: A quick, practical guide to Qanat Systems.

hook.text: In ancient Persia, farmers tapped mountain groundwater using tunnels that ran for miles—without any pumps.

buildup.text: A qanat is a gently sloping underground channel that carries water downhill by gravity alone.

discovery.text: Workers dug vertical shafts every 50 meters for access, then connected them with a horizontal tunnel.

twist.text: Because qanats are underground, almost no water evaporates. In a desert, that efficiency is everything.

climax.text: Some qanats built 3,000 years ago still flow today. They're some of the most durable infrastructure ever made.

punchline.text: No pumps, no power, no evaporation—just gravity and genius.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of qanat irrigation systems?
options: Underground channels prevent evaporation and run on gravity alone
